subject: Private footprint feasibility: packaging options & team impact
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Private footprint feasibility: packaging options & team impact

Team —

Following the Greenbank intake call last week, they asked us for a short feasibility write-up covering packaging options (container images vs. airgap OVA vs. operator install), what each option means for the runtime dependencies, and an estimate of engineering + SRE effort to support each path. I pulled together a quick matrix (attached) but need alignment across product, infra, and solutions before we share anything externally.

High level asks: 
- Can infra confirm which packaging options are realistic for us to support in the next 6 months?
- Product: what features (rollouts, canary, KV cache behavior) would degrade or need additional work for each packaging type?
- Solutions/SE: any customer constraints we should call out (airgapped cert rotation, KMS offline integrations, EULA/packaging clauses)?

I've attached a short PDF with the packaging pros/cons and an initial resourcing matrix. Please review and reply with: a) feasibility (yes/no/conditional), b) delta FTE to support pilot + GA, and c) any hard blockers.

I'll collect responses and produce a one-page for Greenbank and a separate internal ask for staffing. Can we get initial replies by end of day Wed?

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 13:09:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Private footprint feasibility: packaging options & team impact

Irene —

Quick infra read:

Summary answers first:
- Containerized (helm / k8s) image-based installs: ✅ Feasible in 6 months with existing operator + small infra automation work. Estimated delta: 0.4 FTE infra lead + 0.6 FTE engineering support for 3 months for install testing, installer CI, and documented EKS/GKE references.
- OVA / airgap appliance image: ⚠️ Conditional — possible but higher friction. Needs an offline installer, image signing flow, and support for customers who cannot reach our artifact registry. Estimated delta: 1.2 FTE infra + 1.0 SRE for 4 months (build/test/signing/pipeline) and separate QA cycles for airgapped flows.
- Bare-metal operator / systemd packages: ❌ Hard blocker for next-6-months unless we reduce scope. We lack stable bare-metal provisioning/testing infra and would need 2.0 FTEs + lab hardware to reach GA.

Technical notes / blockers: 
- KMS/HSM: We can integrate with customer KMS (vault, AWS KMS) but offline HSM integration (FIPS-certified appliances) requires procurement cycles and testing. For airgapped installs we need a process for key import/export and rotation — that is nontrivial.
- Telemetry & metrics: for private installs we must support a reduced telemetry mode; request product define which traces/metrics are must-have (we can implement sampling but some signals are used for autoscaling safety).
- Runtime dependencies: our current runtime uses dynamic linking to CUDA/cuBLAS in hosted—airgap/bare-metal needs a statically-packaged fallback/lib collection or documented GPU driver matrix.

I put rough numbers in the attached resourcing spreadsheet. Happy to sync 30m tomorrow to walk infra constraints.

- Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 15:02:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Private footprint feasibility: packaging options & team impact

Thanks Mina — this is helpful. A few product clarifications to add from my side: 

1) Feature coverage expectations per packaging: 
- Container (k8s): full feature parity for rollouts, KV cache, streaming, and canary. Good default ask from enterprise customers.
- OVA / airgap image: most runtime features supported; advanced observability (tracing hooks that call back to hosted endpoints) will be limited unless customer allows gated outbound endpoints. Function-calling and third-party connectors will need stubbed/local adapters.
- Bare-metal manual installs: we should treat as a restricted subset. No autoscaling, limited KV cache persistence guarantees, and higher latency variance.

2) Security/compliance ask: we should attach a shrink-wrapped SOC2 checklist for Greenbank that explains what evidence we can provide for private installs and where customer responsibility begins. SEs: can you gather likely evidence requests?

3) Timeline ask: product can accept a container-first pilot in 8 weeks if infra signs off on the 0.4 FTE delta and solutions can secure one pilot customer (Greenbank?) within that window. OVA pilot would need ~3 months. Bare-metal is not in our proposed roadmap.

I will prepare a one-pager that maps features -> packaging matrix (will post link).

-Sooj
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:18:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Private footprint feasibility: packaging options & team impact

Irene / team —

Thanks for the breakdown. From Greenbank's side (cc'd) a few clarifications that will determine our preference: 
- We need full control of key material (KMS) and a documented process for offline rotation — that is non-negotiable.
- We prefer not to run Kubernetes across all datacenters. Containerized installs on managed K8s are fine for pilot but long-term they want an appliance option.
- Timeline: pilot start ideally by Sep 1; if container pilot is August-ish that's acceptable. OVA pilot must be mature by Nov for their procurement window.

Could we get a distilled one-pager for procurement that lists: supported packaging, expected SLAs (latency windows), responsibilities (Redwood vs customer), and a list of deliverables per pilot (install docs, operator, upgrade runbook)?

Happy to help with acceptance criteria.

—Mark
Mark Li
Engineering Manager, Frost Systems (partner engineering for Greenbank)

Subject: Re: Private footprint feasibility: packaging options & team impact

All — thanks for quick inputs. Pulling this together:

Decision (proposed for internal sign-off):
- Container (k8s) first pilot: APPROVE (pilot target: Aug 16 start; infra commits 0.4 FTE + 0.6 eng support for 3 months). Product will limit no-outbound traces by default and provide a canary disable switch. SEs to confirm acceptance criteria by next Wed.
- OVA / airgap: CONDITIONAL APPROVAL for R&D and procurement prep. Infra requests 1.2 FTE + 1.0 SRE; timeline ~12 weeks to pilot readiness (target Nov procurement). Product to produce feature-delta doc showing any limitations.
- Bare-metal manual installs: REJECT for current roadmap (defer to H2 '27 with dedicated lab investment).

Action items (owners / dates):
1) Product (Soojin) — one-pager for procurement w/ feature matrix & responsibilities (due 2026-06-17). Link to doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDEFG-packaging-notes
2) Infra (Mina) — confirm FTE allocation and upload updated resourcing spreadsheet (due 2026-06-15).
3) Solutions/SE (Jasmine) — draft SOC2 evidence map for private installs + list of customer responsibilities for airgap (due 2026-06-17).
4) Partner (Mark/Greenbank) — confirm pilot window and acceptance criteria (Greenbank to reply by 2026-06-18).

I'll convert this to a short internal decision memo for exec review and include estimated cost delta. If nobody objects within 48 hours I'll mark as approved and open INFRA-3921 for the container pilot work.

Thanks —
Karthik
